subject: MSA / Order Form - Auto-renew override request & termination-for-convenience playbook
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@atlascloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: opt-out of auto-renew for pilot + notice window clarification

Hi Jonas / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the recent pilot run — team is happy with latency and cost so far. Procurement has surfaced two items we need finalized before we can sign the order form: 

1) Can Redwood add an explicit one-time "pilot opt-out" exception to the Order Form that prevents auto-renew on pilot SKUs? Procurement wants this in writing (they've seen auto-renew bite them previously).
2) If termination for convenience (TFC) remains in the MSA, they want a defined notice window (30 days preferred) and clarity on whether a TFC triggers refund/credit for unused committed capacity.

I've attached a short note from their legal team outlining the risk concerns (Attachment: Atlas_Renewal_Request.pdf).

Are these things we can do without a full MSA amendment? If not, happy to schedule a quick call to walk legal/procurement through options.

Thanks,
Helen
Helen Park
Director, Cloud Procurement
AtlasCloud

(Attachment: Atlas_Renewal_Request.pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Helen Park <helen.park@atlascloud.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: opt-out of auto-renew for pilot + notice window clarification

Marissa — forwarding a request from AtlasCloud (attached). Procurement asks for a one-time pilot opt-out from auto-renew and a 30-day TFC notice with clear refund/credit rules for unused committed capacity.

Quick context: this is a relatively small pilot (3 GPU reserved instances) but they want written assurance they won't auto-renew into a larger committed period. Sales would prefer to handle with an Order Form amendment or a short-side letter rather than changing the MSA broadly.

Can you advise: 
- Whether we can do an Order Form addendum limited to the pilot that overrides auto-renew on pilot SKUs?
- If TFC stays in MSA, recommended language for 30-day notice and how to handle pre-paid or reserved capacity credits?

If it's easier, let's book 30 minutes; Kimberly will help operationalize the amendment.

Thanks — Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Helen Park <helen.park@atlascloud.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: opt-out of auto-renew for pilot + notice window clarification

Thanks for the context. Read the attachment — reasonable ask for a pilot. High-level guidance below; attaching a redline (MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a proposed Order Form amendment snippet.

1) Pilot-only auto-renew carve-out: feasible via an Order Form amendment (short-side letter) that explicitly states: 
   "Notwithstanding Section X (Auto-Renewal) of the MSA, the pilot SKUs described in Order Form #PF-8241 shall not auto-renew upon the end of the pilot term. Any continuation of service shall require a mutually executed successor Order Form."

   This language avoids wholesale MSA changes and is limited to the Order Form ID. Sales should ensure the Order Form includes the SKU identifiers and pilot period dates.

2) Termination for Convenience (TFC) notice and credits: we can keep TFC in the MSA but clarify in the Order Form amendment that: 
   - TFC requires 30 days written notice.
   - If Customer elects TFC during a pre-paid/committed period, Redwood will provide a pro rata credit for unused prepaid months based on the agreed committed fees, less any non-refundable setup fees.

   Draft clause included in the redline: 
   "If Customer terminates for convenience, Redwood will calculate a pro rata refund or credit for any prepaid, unused portion of committed capacity fees, subject to deduction of non-refundable implementation fees explicitly listed in the Order Form."

3) Operational runbook: Kimberly, if sales wants to approve this, operations needs: 1) clear SKU list, 2) pilot end date, 3) billing contact, 4) migration/transfer plan if they later move to Dedicated. Suggest we attach a short runbook as an appendix to the amendment.

Next steps I recommend:
- Jonas/Kimberly: confirm you want to proceed with Order Form amendment (one-off) vs MSA amendment (broad).
- If one-off: Kimberly to populate SKU list and pilot dates; I will prepare DocuSign amendment and include the redline.
- If MSA-level change is required (rare), route to Legal for full approval — longer lead time.

I'll prepare the amendment draft today. Attaching MSA_redline_v3.docx and a sample amendment.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: MSA_redline_v3.docx)
